title: Why invest in property instead of shares, gold or other options?
excerpt: Shares, bonds, gold and savings plans all compete for your money. Sean gives three reasons he favours property, leverage, slow and visible trends, and rent along the way, while still urging diversification.

question.context: Investors can choose shares, bonds, insurance savings plans, gold, commodities or cryptocurrency. Sean has invested in shares and businesses too, and was asked why he still focuses on property.
question.text: Why choose property over other investments?

answer.quote: you use minimum to get maximum
answer.summary: Sean gives three reasons: banks lend you most of the price, property trends move slowly enough to see and act on, and the property pays rent while you hold it. But he still says not to put all your eggs in one basket.

reasons.title: Leverage from the bank
reasons.body: On a RM500,000 home you pay about RM50,000 and the bank lends RM450,000. Sell at RM600,000 and your RM50,000 has made RM100,000, with housing loans charging up to about 5%.

reasons.title: Trends move slowly
reasons.body: When a new rail line opens, you can watch people move along it over years. Share prices can fall overnight on news from abroad.

reasons.title: Rent while you wait
reasons.body: Gold just sits until you sell it. A property earns rent every month for years, and you can still sell it at the end.

actions: Compare how much of each investment you can finance with a loan.
Follow infrastructure and population moves to spot slow trends early.
Count rental income, not just the sale price, in your returns.
Spread your money: for RM1 million, Sean suggests about RM600,000 in property and the rest in shares, bonds, business and yourself.
Spread properties across price ranges and places, not one block.
caveat: Sean says property suits his personality and work; other investors may do better with shares. The loan rate of up to about 5% is as he stated it in 2017.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this October 2017 video. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. His example of buying a new launch with a 1% deposit is left out, as such schemes may no longer apply.
